subject: maths
chapterTitle: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
title: What a pair of linear equations is

goals: Say what a linear equation in two variables is
Check whether a pair (x, y) is a solution
Tell from the numbers how many solutions there are

cards.title: A linear equation in two variables
cards.body:
It can be written as **ax + by + c = 0**, where a, b and c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero.

Example: 2x + 3y = 12. A solution is a pair (x, y) that makes it true, like (3, 2), because 2(3) + 3(2) = 12.

cards.title: A pair of them
cards.body:
Two such equations in the same x and y make a **pair of linear equations**:

x + y = 7
x − y = 1

A solution of the pair must satisfy **both** at once. x = 4, y = 3 works: 4 + 3 = 7 and 4 − 3 = 1.

cards.question: Is (2, 1) a solution of the pair x + 2y = 4 and 2x − y = 3?
cards.why: Check each one: 2 + 2(1) = 4 is true, and 2(2) − 1 = 3 is true. A solution has to satisfy both equations, and (2, 1) does.

cards.title: Each equation is a straight line
cards.body:
Plot every solution of one linear equation and they all fall on a straight line.

So a pair of equations is a pair of lines, and a solution of the pair is a point that lies on both lines.

cards.title: Three ways two lines can sit

cards.question: The two lines of a pair of equations are parallel. How many solutions does the pair have?
cards.why: Parallel lines never meet, so no point lies on both of them. The pair has no solution, and we call it inconsistent.

cards.title: Tell from the numbers alone
cards.remember: Write both equations as ax + by + c = 0 before comparing.

cards.question: How many solutions does the pair x + 2y − 4 = 0 and 2x + 4y − 12 = 0 have?
cards.why: a₁/a₂ = 1/2 and b₁/b₂ = 2/4 = 1/2, but c₁/c₂ = −4/−12 = 1/3. The first two ratios match and the third doesn't, so the lines are parallel and there is no solution.

points: A solution of a pair satisfies both equations
Each equation is a line: intersecting, parallel or coincident
Compare a₁/a₂, b₁/b₂ and c₁/c₂ to know how many solutions
